newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norsk Hydro to run idle aluminium capacity.
newsitem.headline: Norsk Hydro to run idle aluminium capacity.

text.p: Norwegian industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA said on Monday it planned to phase in all previously idle aluminium production capacity in the third quarter.
"It is correct that we no longer wish to have idle production capacity for aluminium," Odd Gullberg, a spokesman for Hydro, told Reuters.
Hydro previously announced that it would increase primary aluminium output by 20,000 tonnes in the first quarter 1997 and would continue to add capacity according to market conditions.
The company's production was around 675,000 tonnes at the end of 1996.
"By end of the 1997 our capacity will be 740,000 tonnes per year, including new additional capacity from investments at Aardal and Karmoey," said Thomas Knutzen, a spokesman for Hydro Aluminium.
He added that the new investments would add about 47,000 tonnes to annual production and would come on stream during the autumn.

"We have continued to start up extra production according to regulations and customers needs," Knutzen said. "We've had fairly strong demand from our customers and we reqire additional production to serve their needs."
